card.law_is_about: The annual package of German tax changes.
card.they_want: Convert employee-tax thresholds into allowances and simplify staff-event taxation.
card.they_claim: The €110 staff-event rule is a threshold whose small excess can cause disproportionate tax.
card.the_problem: The cited income-tax provision already exempts the first €110 for qualifying events.

claim_quote.translation_en: Translation of fragment: exemption thresholds (e.g. the €110 limit for staff events

request_quote.translation_en: Translation of request fragment: be designed as allowances

counter_quote.original: Soweit solche Zuwendungen den Betrag von 110 Euro je Betriebsveranstaltung und teilnehmenden Arbeitnehmer nicht übersteigen
counter_quote.translation_en: Translation of fragment: To the extent that such benefits do not exceed €110 per staff event and participating employee

locator.section: §19(1) sentence 1 no 1a, sentence 3; sentence 4 limits this to two annual events

correction: For qualifying events, only the excess above €110 is employment income. The €50 benefits-in-kind example is a genuine threshold; this finding concerns only the €110 example.
effect: Weakens one stated cliff-edge rationale for changing existing income-tax rules.
materiality: Minor: one example in a broader reform programme is wrong. It implies a tax cliff where the cited provision already supplies the requested allowance.
direction_explanation: The misdescription supports the stated aim of preventing disproportionate tax when a limit is narrowly exceeded.
limits: Does not establish that event administration is simple or that the separate10% flat-tax proposal is unwise. VAT has a different €110 threshold; the passage expressly cites income-tax §19. Eligibility conditions and the two-event limit still apply.
alternative_explanations: The author may have used Freigrenze loosely for monetary limits generally. The explicit request for conversion to Freibeträge, linked to small excesses, makes that wording consequential.
The following page discusses differing VAT and wage-tax treatment, but does not qualify the cited income-tax example.

additional_evidence.note: The pre-existing 2025 ministry table expressly classifies the €110 rule as a Freibetrag. Official indexed text read; live archival request failed503.

reading_extent: All 13 author pages read; page 11 visually checked. Current §19 and dated 2025 official table checked, plus exact government draft article list/operative search.
